ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black/dark grey) across ~95% of the visible surface with high-intensity (white) localized pixel spikes corresponding to scarring and barnacle colonization.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Continuous dark-toned region across both lobes. High-contrast white clusters localized at the distal tips of both left and right lobes. Scattered linear and circular white-pixel anomalies distributed primarily across the left-central and right-mid regions.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped depression with a deep vertical penetration into the fluke body; narrow angular convergence at the base.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations across the entire trailing edge. Visible peak-and-valley variations with higher amplitude closer to the outer tips; more subtle micro-serrations toward the median notch.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Trailing edge follows a generally concave path from the outer tips toward the median notch, with irregular pixel-level interruptions due to serration.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Distinct clusters of high-intensity circular pixel groupings (barnacles) localized at the extreme lateral tips of both lobes. A single high-intensity circular spot is located just left of the median notch base.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple high-contrast linear streaks on the left lobe, including one prominent vertical scratch and several unaligned oblique markings. Subtle horizontal linear marks visible on the right lobe surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A prominent circular ring-shaped scar is visible on the central-right lobe. Significant white scarring/pigmentation loss is visible on the upper left margin near the tip.
other_distinctive_markers: Presence of dark, irregular appendages (potential organic debris or seaweed) clinging to the far left distal tip.
